name: TablePlus
tagline: Free, open source TablePlus alternative for Mac.
description: TablePlus is $99 a device and closed source. TablePro is free, open source under AGPLv3, and covers 25 databases. Both are native Mac apps — that part is a tie.
longDescription: TablePlus is the closest thing to TablePro on the Mac: a genuinely native AppKit app, fast, well made, and shipping since 2019. It also has an LLM chat panel and, since June 2026, an MCP server — so the usual "native versus Electron" and "we have AI" arguments do not apply here. What separates them is the licence. TablePlus costs $99 for one device or $129 for two, includes one year of updates, and asks $59 per device to keep receiving them. TablePro is free, AGPLv3, and the source is public.
prosTablePro: Six Safe Mode levels, set per connection
prosCompetitor: Perpetual licence — your last covered build keeps working
chooseTablePro: you want the same native Mac experience without a per-device licence, or you want to read the source.
chooseCompetitor: you need Windows or Linux, you already own a licence, or you prefer paying once for a build you can freeze.
verdict: TablePlus is a good native Mac client and the closest match to TablePro in design and speed. The difference is not performance and it is no longer AI — both ship an MCP server. It is the licence: $99 a device and closed, against free and AGPLv3.
ogCompetitorMetaHtml:
$99 per device
+$59 to keep updates
Closed source
ogPunchline: Both native. One is free and open source.

migrationSteps.title: Open the importer
migrationSteps.description: File > Import Connections, then pick TablePlus. The Setapp edition is detected as well, and TablePlus does not need to be running.

migrationSteps.title: Passwords come across
migrationSteps.description: Connections, groups, SSH tunnels and SSL settings are read directly, and passwords are copied from the macOS Keychain into your own Keychain.

migrationSteps.title: Check the tunnels
migrationSteps.description: Open one connection that uses an SSH tunnel and connect once. Everything else carries over untouched, so nothing needs retyping.

faqs.question: Is TablePro slower than TablePlus?
faqs.answer: No, and neither is meaningfully slower than the other. Both are native Mac apps — TablePro in SwiftUI and AppKit, TablePlus in AppKit — so neither pays the startup or memory cost of Electron or a JVM. Anyone claiming a large speed gap between two native clients is guessing.

faqs.question: Does TablePlus have AI and MCP?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. TablePlus ships an LLM chat panel that you point at OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub Copilot or a local model, and it added an MCP server in version 7.1.8 on 10 June 2026. TablePro has the same two capabilities. This is not a difference between them.

faqs.question: Why do you say 16 databases when TablePlus documents 13?
faqs.answer: Their documentation lists 13 engines and their homepage shows 14 logos, and the two lists do not match — BigQuery, ClickHouse and Turso appear only on the homepage, Snowflake and Vertica only in the docs. Sixteen is the union of both, which is the most generous reading. TablePro ships 25 drivers.

faqs.question: What does the TablePlus licence actually cost over time?
faqs.answer: A licence is $99 for one device or $129 for two, one time, and includes a year of updates. After that the app keeps working forever on the last build your term covered, with no feature lockout. To carry on receiving updates it is $59 per device. The bundled iOS unlock, however, stops when the term lapses.

faqs.question: Can I import my TablePlus connections?
faqs.answer: Yes. TablePro reads TablePlus connections directly, including the Setapp edition, and takes passwords from the macOS Keychain along with SSH tunnels and SSL settings. TablePlus does not need to be running, and groups and folders carry over.

name: DBeaver
tagline: Free, Native DBeaver Alternative for Mac.
description: Native DBeaver alternative for Mac. 80 MB RAM, instant startup, no Java. Free and open source. 25 databases.
longDescription: DBeaver is a popular cross-platform database tool licensed Apache 2.0. The Community Edition is free; DBeaver PRO starts at $99 per year. It runs on Java 21 via the Eclipse RCP. On Mac you'll see 8+ second cold starts and 800 MB of RAM at idle on the same connections where TablePro starts in 1 second and idles at 80 MB.
prosTablePro: Cold start under 1 second vs ~8 seconds
AI SQL assistant in the free tier
prosCompetitor: 100+ database drivers in the Community Edition
Mature feature set after a decade of releases
chooseTablePro: you want a Mac-native app with a one-second start and 80 MB of RAM, free, with AI built in.
chooseCompetitor: you need a database TablePro doesn't yet support, or you work across Linux and Windows often.
verdict: DBeaver is solid on every OS. TablePro is faster and lighter on Mac because it skips Java. Pick the one that matches where you work.

migrationSteps.title: Install TablePro
migrationSteps.description: brew install --cask tablepro. DBeaver stays installed.

migrationSteps.title: Import from DBeaver
migrationSteps.description: File > Import from Other App > DBeaver. TablePro reads the workspace at ~/Library/DBeaverData/, decrypts credentials-config.json, and previews every connection.

migrationSteps.title: Confirm import
migrationSteps.description: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, MariaDB, Cassandra all map. JDBC-only drivers (Db2, Teradata, etc.) skip with a warning.

faqs.question: Why is DBeaver so slow on Mac?
faqs.answer: DBeaver runs on the Eclipse RCP, a Java desktop framework. JVM startup, SWT widget rendering, and JDBC each add overhead. TablePro skips all of that with native libpq, libmariadb, hiredis.

faqs.question: Does TablePro support as many databases?
faqs.answer: DBeaver supports 100+ via JDBC. TablePro supports 18 via native drivers. The 18 cover Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and the major cloud databases.

faqs.question: Can I migrate connections from DBeaver?
faqs.answer: Yes. File > Import from Other App > DBeaver. Connections and folder structure transfer. Passwords need re-entry due to DBeaver project-key encryption.

faqs.question: Is TablePro really 10 times lighter?
faqs.answer: RAM idle: 80 MB vs DBeaver's 800 MB on the same connections. Cold start: 1 second vs 8 seconds. Measured on M2 Mac.

faqs.question: What about DBeaver Pro features?
faqs.answer: DBeaver Pro adds NoSQL support, ER diagrams, and visual query builder for $25 a month. TablePro includes ER diagrams, Mongo, Redis, and AI in the free tier.

name: DataGrip
tagline: Free, Native DataGrip Alternative for Mac.
description: Native DataGrip alternative for Mac. Free, open source, fast. JetBrains-quality editor without the IntelliJ weight.
longDescription: DataGrip is JetBrains' database IDE, built on the IntelliJ platform in Java. It costs $99 the first year, $79 the second, $59 from year three; or $9.90 per month. TablePro is free, native macOS, and starts in 1 second. Same SQL editor power for daily work, without the IDE weight.
chooseTablePro: you want a fast, free, native Mac client and don't need Git inside the SQL editor.
chooseCompetitor: you live in the JetBrains ecosystem and need Git integration and refactoring tools in the same window.
verdict: DataGrip is a full IDE. TablePro is a tight client that does daily database work better and free.

migrationSteps.title: Install TablePro
migrationSteps.description: brew install --cask tablepro. DataGrip stays installed in parallel.

migrationSteps.title: Re-enter your data sources
migrationSteps.description: DataGrip stores connections in IDE settings. Recreate each in TablePro by hand or paste the JDBC URL.

migrationSteps.title: Move daily work over
migrationSteps.description: Keep DataGrip for refactoring and Git tasks. Use TablePro for everything else, especially the parts where startup time matters.

faqs.question: Will TablePro replace DataGrip for me?
faqs.answer: For everyday SQL work, schema browsing, data editing: yes. For SQL refactoring across files and migrations comparison: no, those stay DataGrip strengths.

faqs.question: Why is DataGrip so heavy?
faqs.answer: It's the full IntelliJ platform. JVM, plugin sandbox, code intelligence services. Every database tool inherits the IDE weight.

faqs.question: Is TablePro really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. Optional paid license to support development; no feature gating.

faqs.question: Does TablePro have version control?
faqs.answer: Not inside the editor. Save queries to .sql files in your repo, version them with git like any other source code.

faqs.question: Can I use both DataGrip and TablePro?
faqs.answer: Yes. They don't conflict. Many devs use TablePro for daily browsing, DataGrip for migration reviews.

name: Navicat

longDescription: Navicat Premium covers 7+ databases in one app. It costs $399 per year subscription or $1,299 for a perpetual license per user. TablePro covers 25 databases and is free, open source under AGPLv3. Native macOS, no per-database editions.

prosCompetitor: Mature data modeler with reverse engineering
Data sync between tables and instances

chooseCompetitor: you need Navicat-only features like Data Modeler reverse engineering or a built-in job scheduler.
verdict: Navicat does more for $30 a month. TablePro does the everyday 80% for free.

$0 Lifetime
SwiftUI · open source
One app, every DB

migrationSteps.title: Install TablePro
migrationSteps.description: brew install --cask tablepro.

migrationSteps.title: Import Navicat connections
migrationSteps.description: File > Import from Other App > Navicat reads .ncx and migrates connection metadata. Passwords need re-entry.

migrationSteps.title: Cancel the subscription
migrationSteps.description: Once everything works in TablePro, cancel Navicat. Save $360 a year per database.

faqs.question: Will TablePro replace Navicat?
faqs.answer: For everyday querying, browsing, editing, importing, exporting, SSH, schema design: yes. For Navicat's Data Modeler reverse engineering, Data Sync, Job Scheduler: not yet.

faqs.question: Can I import Navicat connections?
faqs.answer: Yes. TablePro reads .ncx connection files. Connection metadata transfers; passwords need re-entry.

faqs.question: Is TablePro really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. No subscription. Optional paid license to support development.

faqs.question: What about Navicat for Oracle's PL/SQL debugger?
faqs.answer: Navicat for Oracle is more mature there. TablePro handles SQL queries and basic schema browsing well; PL/SQL package debugging isn't there yet.

faqs.question: Can I use both?
faqs.answer: Yes. They don't conflict. Try TablePro alongside Navicat and switch when ready.

name: Beekeeper Studio
tagline: Native Beekeeper Studio Alternative for Mac.
description: Native Beekeeper Studio alternative for Mac. 4x lighter, native Swift, no Electron. Free and open source.
longDescription: Beekeeper Studio is a friendly cross-platform database client built on Electron. The Community Edition is free; paid tiers start at $108 per year (Indie) and add AI from the Professional tier ($168 per year). Electron bundles Chromium so even at idle the app uses 200-400 MB of RAM. TablePro is native SwiftUI for Mac. 80 MB at idle, under 1 second to start.
prosTablePro: 80 MB RAM vs ~200-400 MB for Electron
AI SQL assistant in the free tier (Beekeeper requires Pro)
chooseTablePro: you work mainly on Mac and want a real native app instead of a Chromium runtime.
chooseCompetitor: you split time between Mac, Linux, and Windows and want feature parity across all three.
verdict: Beekeeper Studio is the best Electron-based DB client. TablePro is the best Mac-native one.
ogPunchline: Native Swift. No Chromium runtime. 4x lighter.

migrationSteps.title: Install TablePro
migrationSteps.description: brew install --cask tablepro. Beekeeper stays installed.

migrationSteps.title: Re-enter your connections
migrationSteps.description: Beekeeper stores connections in its own format. Recreate each in TablePro or paste the connection URL.

migrationSteps.title: Compare for a week
migrationSteps.description: Run both side by side. The startup speed and RAM difference are obvious by day three.

faqs.question: Why is Beekeeper Studio heavier than TablePro?
faqs.answer: It's built on Electron, which bundles Chromium. Even an idle Electron app is hundreds of MB of RAM. TablePro is native SwiftUI; idle stays at 80 MB.

faqs.question: Does TablePro work on Apple Silicon?
faqs.answer: Yes. Universal Binary, native arm64 and x86_64. Beekeeper Studio runs on M-series via the bundled Chromium.

faqs.question: Is TablePro really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source. Beekeeper has a free Community Edition too; both are honest about that.

faqs.question: Can I import Beekeeper connections?
faqs.answer: Not yet. TablePro doesn't read Beekeeper's connection store. Recreate connections by hand.

faqs.question: Does TablePro work on Linux and Windows?
faqs.answer: No. TablePro is Mac-native by design. If you need cross-platform, Beekeeper Studio is the pragmatic pick.

name: Sequel Pro
tagline: Modern Sequel Pro Alternative for Mac.

prosCompetitor: Familiar UI for Sequel Pro veterans
Free and open source (MIT, Sequel Ace)
chooseTablePro: you want active development, multi-database support, and modern macOS features like iCloud sync.
chooseCompetitor: you only use MySQL and prefer the Sequel Pro UI you already know.

name: Azimutt

prosTablePro: Full database client with SQL editor and data grid
Edit data inline, run queries, manage table structure
prosCompetitor: Built for very large schemas (1000+ tables)
chooseTablePro: you need a real database client to query, edit, and manage data, plus ER diagrams for moderate schemas.

name: phpMyAdmin
description: Native phpMyAdmin alternative for Mac. SSH-tunneled, no public web surface. Free and open source. 25 databases.
longDescription: phpMyAdmin is a free GPL-licensed PHP web app for MySQL and MariaDB. The current release (5.2.x as of late 2025) ships with most cPanel hosts. It's a recurring CVE target when exposed publicly. TablePro is a desktop client. SSH-tunnel through your existing server access; no public web surface.
prosTablePro: No public web surface to attack
Native macOS UX with Touch ID and dark mode
chooseTablePro: you ssh to your servers and want a real desktop client.
chooseCompetitor: you only have browser access to your server (no SSH) or use shared hosting.
verdict: phpMyAdmin is the default on shared hosts. TablePro is the safer, faster choice when SSH is on the table.

migrationSteps.title: Install TablePro on your Mac
migrationSteps.description: brew install --cask tablepro. Nothing to install on the server.

migrationSteps.title: Add an SSH-tunneled connection
migrationSteps.description: New Connection > MySQL. Fill DB credentials. Open the SSH tab and add your bastion or server credentials.

migrationSteps.title: Block /phpmyadmin in nginx
migrationSteps.description: Once TablePro works, deny public access to /phpmyadmin in nginx or Apache. SSH tunneling replaces it.

faqs.question: Why move from phpMyAdmin?
faqs.answer: Two reasons: security (phpMyAdmin is a recurring CVE target when exposed) and UX (a real desktop app beats a web form). If you can SSH, you can stop exposing /phpmyadmin.

faqs.question: Does TablePro need a server install?
faqs.answer: No. TablePro runs on your Mac. Connects to MySQL directly or through SSH.

faqs.question: Can I tunnel through a bastion?
faqs.answer: Yes. Password, key, or agent. Jump hosts and custom ports work.

faqs.question: Will I lose phpMyAdmin features?
faqs.answer: Core ones, no: SQL editor, table browser, structure editor, import/export, query history. Some niche features (designer view, GIS plot) aren't in TablePro yet.

faqs.question: Is TablePro free like phpMyAdmin?
faqs.answer: Yes. AGPLv3 open source.
